rounds.agent_text: for x=11.36 showed the 60-digit run was ALSO wrong (1174 ULP from reference), indicating a logic error not rounding. When x > 10, `dgamma(x)` uses the asymptotic formula `exp((y-0.5)*log(y) - y + sq2pil + d9lgmc(y))`, which produces a large value. Inverting that large value (1/GAMMA(11.36)) loses precision. The correct approach for DGAMR when |x| > 10 is to compute the reciprocal directly via `exp(-log(GAMMA(x)))`, which the log-gamma path does. My Round 2 change incorrectly sent all positive x through direct inversion; this restores the original Fortran's threshold at |x| = 10 for both signs.
